title: Realize any strict finite scalar passband union by a positive passive star
statement: Given S=4K>0 and 0=alpha0<beta0<alpha1<beta1<...<alpha(n-1)<beta(n-1), q(t)=(product(t+beta)/product(t+alpha)-1)/S is a positive Stieltjes sum. Its residues and interlacing zeros construct a positive star with n active degrees of freedom, backbone mass m and n-1 side masses and springs, realizing exactly the prescribed full bands.

requires: Finite strict interlacing squared endpoints, alpha0=0, S=4K>0
provides: 1/m=(sum beta-sum alpha)/S; 1/M=product beta/(S product of positive alpha)
At each zero -sigma of q, rho=1/(-sigma q'(-sigma))>0 gives side mass rho/sigma and spring rho
Trace/log resources suffice for strict finite-band spectra; common dark/touching factors may be cancelled
Minimal active star has n-1 branches; expansion gives backbone incident stiffness
assumptions: Classical Foster/Stieltjes/Cauer inverse synthesis ancestry is credited; no new synthesis principle claimed
Active scalar response need not identify hardware or invisible dark modes
costs: Explicit residues and n-1 interlacing zero isolations
Narrow pole/zero gaps can demand high precision, small masses or high frequencies; no robustness/affordability guarantee
contract.units: alpha/beta/sigma are squared angular frequencies; recovered masses/springs use supplied stiffness scale S
contract.obstruction: Exact attainable-spectrum realization for the bulk scalar model; no vector, multichannel, contact or material constraints acquired.

evidence.range_scope: Governing universal family v3, including zero-coefficient and dimensionless-log clarifications.

body: The inverse operation is useful separately from Bose optimization and retains established synthesis attribution.

review.scope: Actual completed audit is a separate version-bound overlay.
